title: What is a Verb?
content: A verb is a word that expresses an action, occurrence, or state of being. Every complete sentence must have a verb. Verbs can describe physical actions (run, jump), mental actions (think, believe), or states (is, seem, become).

title: Present Tenses
content: Present Simple describes habits and general truths: 'She walks the dog every morning.' Present Continuous describes actions happening right now: 'The cat is sleeping on the windowsill.' Use 'is/am/are + verb-ing' for present continuous.

title: Past Tenses
content: Past Simple describes completed actions: 'They finished their homework yesterday.' Past Continuous describes ongoing past actions, often interrupted: 'She was cooking dinner when I called.' Past Perfect describes actions completed before another past action: 'They had gone to the store before it closed.'

title: Future Tenses
content: Future Simple describes actions that will happen: 'He will sing at the concert tomorrow.' Future Continuous describes ongoing future actions: 'He will be singing at the concert.' Future Perfect describes actions that will be completed before a future point: 'By next year, I will have finished my degree.' Present Continuous can also describe planned future actions: 'We are going to Paris next summer.'

title: Present Perfect
content: Present Perfect connects a past action to the present moment. Use 'have/has + past participle.' Use it for: experiences ('We have seen this movie before'), recent actions with present consequences ('I have lost my keys'), and actions in an unfinished time period ('He has drunk three cups of coffee today').
